answer: Each grader holds a forward-secure ephemeral credential: a one-time signing key at the tip of a 16-link hash chain, rotated at every epoch summit. Past tips cannot sign new grades, so a stolen key dies after one window. An island of N fakes still needs N live tip ceremonies every epoch, so attacker cost grows linearly with swarm size. Weakness: honest graders who miss the rotation sit out until the next tip. A zephyr of short-lived keys keeps compromise local.
